title: Why the First Jet Planes Broke Apart in the Sky #shorts

cast.jet: a sleek plain silver 1950s jet airliner with four engines tucked inside its wings and small square-cornered windows, bare unpainted metal with no logos, no markings and no lettering
cast.engineer: a tall engineer in a white lab coat and round glasses with short gray hair
cast.panel: a curved silver riveted aluminum plane skin panel with one sharp square-cornered window hole
cast.passenger: a young woman in a cozy mustard-yellow sweater with a dark brown ponytail

lines.text: Why did the world's first jet passenger planes keep breaking apart in the sky?
lines.label: THE MYSTERY
lines.headline: JETS BREAKING APART
lines.image: {jet} flying high above white clouds, a thin dark crack running across its silver body, tense dramatic sky

lines.text: In 1952, this sleek new jet began carrying passengers high above the clouds.
lines.label: THE NEW JET
lines.headline: FIRST JET PASSENGERS, 1952
lines.image: {jet} gliding high above fluffy white clouds in a bright blue sky, sunlight gleaming on its silver body, hopeful proud mood

lines.text: Then in 1954, two of them broke apart over the sea while still climbing.
lines.label: THE CRASHES
lines.headline: TWO JETS LOST, 1954
lines.image: {jet} breaking apart in mid-air high over a deep blue sea, silver pieces tumbling toward the water, dramatic stormy light

lines.text: All those jets were kept on the ground, and nobody knew why.
lines.label: GROUNDED
lines.headline: NOBODY KNEW WHY
lines.image: a row of three of {jet} parked still on an empty gray runway under a cloudy sky, no people around, quiet worried mood

lines.text: So engineers sank a whole plane body into a giant tank of water.
lines.label: THE TANK
lines.headline: A PLANE IN A TANK
lines.image: {engineer} standing beside a giant indoor water tank inside a huge hangar, a long wingless silver plane body lying submerged in the clear blue water of the tank, curious mood

lines.text: Again and again, they pumped water in and out, like flight after flight.
lines.label: THE PUMPING
lines.headline: FLIGHT AFTER FLIGHT
lines.image: {engineer} turning a big red valve wheel on thick pipes that run into a giant indoor water tank holding a long silver plane body, water swirling, busy determined mood

lines.text: Finally, the metal split open right at one sharp, square corner.
lines.label: THE CRACK
lines.headline: IT SPLIT AT A CORNER
lines.image: close-up of {panel}, a jagged dark crack splitting the silver metal open from one sharp square corner of the hole, dramatic shocking mood

lines.text: Each flight's air pressure stretched that corner a tiny bit, until the metal tore.
lines.label: THE STRETCH
lines.headline: PRESSURE STRETCHED IT
lines.image: close-up of {panel} bulging slightly outward, soft glowing arrows of air pushing on it, a small tear opening at one sharp square corner of the hole, serious mood

lines.text: Their test solved it: round corners spread the stretch out, keeping the metal strong.
lines.label: THE FIX
lines.headline: ROUND CORNERS WIN
lines.image: {engineer} smiling proudly in a workshop, holding up a silver window frame with smooth round corners, a cracked square-cornered frame lying on the workbench beside him, warm triumphant light

lines.text: That's why the window by your airplane seat has round corners, not square ones.
lines.label: YOUR WINDOW
lines.headline: LOOK AT YOUR WINDOW
lines.image: {passenger} sitting in a modern airplane window seat, smiling and touching the smooth rounded corner of an oval plane window, white clouds and blue sky outside, cozy warm light

description:
Why did the world's first jet passenger planes keep breaking apart in the sky?
